questions.question: The imaginary plane passing through the bony prominences marked in red in the image below lies at the level of ______.

suspectLines.text: The structures marked in red are the tubercles of the iliac crest. An imaginary line passing through them forms the trans-tubercular plane, which lies at the upper border of L5.

questions.explanation:
The structures marked in red are the tubercles of the iliac crest. An imaginary line passing through them forms the trans-tubercular plane, which lies at the upper border of L5.

The abdomen is divided into nine regions by two transverse planes and two vertical planes. The subcostal plane joins the lowest points of the costal margins and corresponds to the 10th costal cartilage and lower border of L2/upper border of L3. The trans-tubercular plane joins the iliac-crest tubercles and corresponds to L5. The right and left lateral planes run from the midclavicular point to the mid-inguinal point.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is not present in the plane marked as 1 in the image?

suspectLines.text: The transpyloric (Addison's) plane passes midway between the suprasternal notch and upper border of the pubic symphysis, corresponding anteriorly to midway between the xiphisternal joint and umbilicus. Posteriorly it crosses the lower half of the L1 body/lower border of L1.

questions.explanation:
The structure marked in the image is the transpyloric plane, present at the L1 level. The origin of the celiac trunk (T12) and the lower limit of the spinal cord of a newborn (L3) are not present at this level.

The transpyloric (Addison's) plane passes midway between the suprasternal notch and upper border of the pubic symphysis, corresponding anteriorly to midway between the xiphisternal joint and umbilicus. Posteriorly it crosses the lower half of the L1 body/lower border of L1.

Structures listed by the source at this plane include pylorus of stomach, D1 duodenum, duodenojejunal flexure, fundus of gallbladder, hilum of left kidney (right slightly lower), origin of superior mesenteric artery, origin of renal artery, origin of portal vein behind pancreatic neck, lower limit of adult spinal cord, and cisterna chyli.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the root of the mesentery is false?

suspectLines.text: Structures crossed include third part of duodenum, abdominal aorta, inferior vena cava, right ureter, and right psoas major. Contents include superior mesenteric vessels (jejunal and ileal branches), nerves of the superior mesenteric plexus, lymphatics and regional lymph nodes, connective tissue and fat.

questions.explanation:
The root of the mesentery is approximately 15 cm long. It is crossed by the right ureter and right psoas major and crosses the midline.

The root is the attachment of the small-intestinal mesentery to the posterior abdominal wall. It runs diagonally from the duodenojejunal flexure on the left side of L2 to the right sacroiliac joint. Intestinal attachment is approximately 5-6 m long and the mesentery is about 20 cm broad.

Structures crossed include third part of duodenum, abdominal aorta, inferior vena cava, right ureter, and right psoas major. Contents include superior mesenteric vessels (jejunal and ileal branches), nerves of the superior mesenteric plexus, lymphatics and regional lymph nodes, connective tissue and fat.

questions.question: A 58-year-old woman was undergoing cholecystectomy. During the procedure, the resident accidentally advanced the scissors along the superior border of the epiploic foramen causing injury. Which of the following structures is likely to be injured?

suspectLines.text: The epiploic foramen is a vertical slit about 3 cm long behind the free right border of the lesser omentum connecting the lesser sac with the greater sac.

questions.explanation:
The superior border of the epiploic foramen (foramen of Winslow) is formed by the caudate lobe of the liver and is likely to be injured in this case.

The epiploic foramen is a vertical slit about 3 cm long behind the free right border of the lesser omentum connecting the lesser sac with the greater sac.

Clinical note: the Pringle maneuver compresses the free margin of the lesser omentum to rapidly control bleeding from the hepatic artery and portal vein in liver trauma and surgery.
